statusText: The CME weekend halt still governs the assessment: nothing has quoted NQ since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and nothing will until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about eleven hours past the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail therefore holds at 10% (low), keeping the action EA_ON and the status green - a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than observed extension. What changed this hour is the character of the news rather than its volume. President Trump said he would declare the Strait of Hormuz "a territory of the United States" after defeating Iran, and Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi rejected it near 10:37 UTC with the line that the strait "cannot be seized by tweet, nor by aircraft carrier". Alongside that, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's confirmed plan to unveil "economic isolation, like the world has never seen before" against Iran next week is now corroborated across multiple outlets, and reporting attached to it says the negotiations to reopen the strait remain stalled - which materially weakens the de-escalation leg that a reported Iran-Oman waterway deal supplied in earlier hours. CENTCOM's count of 62 commercial ships redirected by the blockade as of Friday sizes the disruption. Stress firms one point to 53% (elevated) to carry that shift. It firms no further because the cross-asset evidence remains genuinely split: VIX closed Friday at 14.25, less than a point above its 52-week low of 13.38, and the Nasdaq-100 closed down only 0.13% and about 2.3% below its 52-week high. Confidence is 61% (solid) - the new escalation leg is multiply sourced and every other dimension was re-verified this hour, while the price evidence is stale by necessity rather than by omission.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (10%) alone. No venue quotes NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint sits just beyond the horizon at the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, and the danger window brackets that reopen together with its first 90 minutes of price discovery - a full weekend of accumulated headlines expresses there as an opening gap, not as intraday structure. Gap risk is still two-way but the balance shifted slightly this hour. Pulling one way: a U.S. economic-isolation package explicitly promised for next week, a presidential claim of sovereignty over the strait that Tehran has publicly rejected, reopening talks described as stalled, 62 commercial ships redirected by the blockade, a third ADNOC vessel struck in under a week, WTI at $82.40 after a +5% week and +33% year with an IEA deficit warning attached, and a 10Y at 4.70% pressing a 19-month high. Pulling the other: VIX within a point of its 52-week low, an index that closed the week only 0.13% lower and posted a third consecutive higher week, and a Friday tape that absorbed the escalation with a mid-range settle rather than a liquidation. Treat the reopen as a checkpoint to be scored on observed price path, not as a pre-committed direction. The second checkpoint is the Bessent announcement itself, whose date inside next week is not yet fixed and which is therefore deliberately absent from the verified calendar.
headline: Trump claims the Strait, Tehran rejects it and a U.S. "economic isolation" package is set for next week - with no tape to price any of it, Tail holds at 10% on EA_ON while Stress firms to 53%.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from the primary quote page, remains benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, with the session settling mid-range inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide and no close near either extreme. NQ sits about 2.7% below its 52-week high of 30,975.50 against a 52-week low of 22,961.50. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, about 2.3% below its 52-week high. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle, several percent off the highs, is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension and pinning near extremes that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency here is not merely low - it is unmeasurable, because nothing has traded for more than fourteen hours.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close). The split in the evidence is the central fact of this assessment. Equity volatility is calm to the point of complacency: VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60% on the day, inside a 14.18-14.72 range and only 0.87 points above its 52-week low of 13.38 against a 52-week high of 35.30; it is down 30.8% over six months and 4.7% year to date. Rates and energy say the opposite. The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 5bp Friday to 4.70%, approaching the 19-month high of 4.75% set earlier in the week on renewed long-end inflation aversion; the 2-year rose about 3bp to 4.18%, so the curve is steepening rather than signalling a growth scare, with effective fed funds steady at 3.63%. The Federal Reserve H.15 release corroborates the trajectory into Friday with the 2-year at 4.15% and the 10-year at 4.63% on 13 August. WTI settled at $82.40, +1.42% on the day, +5% on the week, +3.52% on the month and +32.95% on the year; Brent at $88.52, +1.67% on the day and +34.43% on the year, with the move explicitly attributed to increased U.S. economic pressure on Iran and an IEA warning of a deeper 2026 global deficit. U.S. national average gasoline is $4.07 a gallon against $3.16 a year ago. Friday's equity weakness was concentrated in semiconductors rather than broad, and the Nasdaq still closed a third consecutive higher week.

GEOPOLITICS (observed, and the only thing moving today). The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed since fighting began on 28 February. This hour brought escalation of a different kind from the vessel strikes that dominated the earlier Saturday runs: President Trump said he would declare the strait "a territory of the United States" after defeating Iran, citing U.S. military control over vessel passage, and Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi rejected the claim near 10:37 UTC, saying the strait "cannot be seized by tweet, nor by aircraft carrier, nor by issuing an order" and that Tehran "neither fears threats nor cowers before displays of power"; the IRGC commander separately claimed "complete and decisive" control of the passage. Treasury Secretary Bessent's plan to apply "measures like have never been seen in the history of economic isolation on a country" next week - a one-two punch pairing financial restrictions with the existing port blockade - is now corroborated by Bloomberg, CNBC and others, and the reporting states that talks to reopen the strait remain stalled. That last point is a genuine correction to the earlier-hours picture, in which a reported Iran-Oman waterway deal supplied the main de-escalation leg. CENTCOM says the blockade had redirected 62 commercial ships as of Friday. On the vessel front, the ADNOC tanker attack that earlier runs placed near 09:54 UTC today is now clearly reported as having occurred Friday evening and surfaced on the wires this morning; it remains the third ADNOC vessel struck in under a week, with fifteen hit cumulatively, one crew member killed and twenty injured, and Qatar, Kuwait, Egypt and Bahrain have condemned it. Elsewhere, Houthi forces fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mokha near 08:45 UTC, and IDF strikes in southern Lebanon continued, with Nabatieh and Ansar overnight and a fresh strike in Deir al-Zahrani near 09:37 UTC killing two and wounding nine.

ASSESSMENT. Tail is held at 10% and stays deep in the low band. Every element the definition asks for - persistent directional efficiency, failed retracements, repeated extension, NQ holding near extremes - is either absent in the last observed session or unobservable in a halted market, and the non-zero level exists to price weekend headline discontinuity that must eventually clear through a gap rather than through intraday structure. That maps to EA_ON and green, and the mapping is mechanical from current Tail alone. Stress firms one point to 53% (elevated). The increment is deliberate and narrow: what accumulated this hour is a stated intent to escalate economically on a timetable inside the coming week, a sovereignty claim over the waterway that Tehran has publicly rejected, and confirmation that the reopening negotiations are stalled - three things that raise the plausible surprise magnitude at the reopen and beyond without producing any observable price path. It is held to one point because the counter-evidence is equally observed and equally fresh: a VIX within a point of its 52-week low and an index down 0.13% on the week's final session do not describe a market braced for a difficult high-volatility environment, and the contract is explicit that conflicting signals should raise Stress rather than Tail. dominantMode is mixed for exactly that reason. Confidence is 61% (solid): NQ futures, VIX, both key Treasury maturities via two independent sources, WTI and Brent, the geopolitical wire across four independent outlets and the seven-day U.S. calendar were each read directly this hour from primary or exchange-quote pages, and the new escalation leg is multiply corroborated rather than single-sourced. The ceiling on confidence is the structural absence of a live price path - a limitation no provider can escape this weekend - not a gap in what was gathered.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-10% throughout, so the action was EA_ON and the status green in every available slot. Tail held 8-9% across Friday's U.S. cash session, where the data landed and produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, then printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress traced a clear event arc: 30-38% through Friday midday, building to 40-44% across the U.S. cash session, then easing to 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. From 06:00 UTC the weekend escalation sequence lifted the series steadily - Tail to 10% and Stress through 48%, 50%, 51% and 52% - as the Mokha barrage, the Lebanon strikes and the vessel-attack reports landed one after another with no tape to absorb them. Confidence ran 30-60%, weakest in Friday's pre-data European hours and settling at 59-60% across the weekend halt. The 20:00 UTC slot on 14 August is unavailable because no successful Claude snapshot was published for that hour; those fields are null and no past opinion has been rewritten.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 11:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 10:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly eleven hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is projected flat at 10% through the Saturday slots, ticking to 11% from 20:00 UTC as the reopen edges into view and to 12% across the Sunday-morning slots; those increments reflect accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to hold at 53% through the European afternoon, ease a single point to 52% across the thin Saturday U.S. hours when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, then firm back to 53% from 20:00 UTC and through 54-55% across Sunday as the unresolved threads converge on the reopen. Confidence drifts from 61% to 57% across the horizon as the last live prints age further without replacement. The material catalyst sits just beyond the horizon: the CME reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery, which the danger window brackets. Inside the horizon the realistic risks are headline-driven - a further Hormuz vessel strike, an Iranian response to the U.S. territorial claim, an early leak of the promised economic-isolation package, or a breakthrough in the stalled reopening talks - each of which would move Stress and the expected gap rather than produce observable one-way structure. The first genuine scheduled checkpoint is Monday's Empire State print at 12:30 UTC; the week's highest-impact dated item is the FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday 19 August, and its highest-impact undated one is the Treasury's Iran package, which is omitted from the calendar because no exact date has been published. The Jackson Hole symposium falls on 27-29 August, outside this seven-day window.
